native_result.query: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other?
native_result.HypoA: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
native_result.HypoB: The -0.9568 factor of BA degree completion is the logistic log-odds coefficient for Black respondents vs White respondents (White as reference, race-by-SES interaction model BA ~ race*SES): Black coef = -0.9568, OR = 0.384, p < 0.001. The two races are therefore Black and White.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded 8773x9 nls_ses_processed.csv (no missing, no duplicates, no weights). 2) Fitted logistic regression BA DEGREE COMPLETED ~ race*SES with White as reference; Black main effect = -0.956778 ≈ -0.9568 (SE .2154, p<.001, OR .3841, 95%CI .2519-.5859). 3) Enumerated all three reference codings; only White-ref Black contrast equals -0.9568 (all other pairs: +/-0.7160, +/-0.2408, +0.9568). 4) Sensitivity: adding sex keeps it near (-0.9592) but adding ability (+0.1351), percentile (-0.7006), family size (-0.3807) or all (+0.4422) breaks the exact match, showing the match is specific to the race*SES specification. 5) Full-sample complete-case unweighted analysis delivered with reproducible script artifact.

sub_hypo.context: Black and White students participating in the NLS.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.

sub_hypo.text: In the logistic race-by-SES interaction model of BA degree completion, the Black-versus-White contrast, with White as the reference, has a log-odds coefficient of -0.9568 (OR = 0.384, p < 0.001).
sub_hypo.context: Full-sample, complete-case, unweighted analysis of 8,773 NLS participants with social background factors and academic resources measured at secondary school graduation; the coefficient match is specific to the BA ~ race*SES specification with White as the reference.
sub_hypo.relations: Logistic regression with race, SES, and their interaction: the Black main-effect coefficient relative to White is -0.956778 (approximately -0.9568; SE = 0.2154, p < 0.001), with OR = 0.3841 and 95% CI = 0.2519–0.5859. Only the White-reference Black contrast matches -0.9568 among the three race-reference codings.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The -0.9568 factor of BA degree completion is the logistic log-odds coefficient for Black respondents vs White respondents (White as reference, race-by-SES interaction model BA ~ race*SES): Black coef = -0.9568, OR = 0.384, p < 0.001. The two races are therefore Black and White.
